inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted weighted-average, FY2026 10-K note (diluted 221,537,458); flat because SBC is fully expensed and no buybacks occur
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash flow statement, share-based payments expense NZ$1.338m (immaterial; NZX-listed, not a US-style equity-comp issuer). No cash tax withheld on net-share settlement disclosed separately
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD flows discounted at a NZD-built WACC: NZ 10yr risk-free ~4.5%, ERP ~6%, levered beta reflecting a capital-intensive, cyclical, moderately-leveraged (2.32x underlying EBITDA ex-lease) rental/tourism operator with FX exposure across NZD/AUD/USD/CAD. House WACC 9.0%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Leases here are predominantly premises (offices/depots), not the rental fleet itself -- the fleet is on-balance-sheet PP&E funded by interest-bearing borrowings ('Purchase of rental assets' NZ$226.1m sits inside operating cash flow per NZ IAS 7, netted there against ex-fleet/vehicle sale proceeds, not as a lease). Full cash lease payment (principal NZ$20.695m + interest NZ$12.871m = NZ$33.566m, 3.9% of revenue) deducted as an explicit opex line below reported (pre-lease) underlying EBITDA; lease liabilities (NZ$211.6m) excluded from net_debt/total_debt, which is interest-bearing borrowings only, matching the company's own primary leverage covenant metric ('net debt excluding lease liabilities'). D&A used for the EBIT/tax build is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (NZ$117.001m total D&A less NZ$26.049m ROU depreciation = NZ$90.952m, 10.7% of revenue) to avoid double-charging the lease.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- FY2026 total equity (NZ$641.083m) equals shareholders' equity exactly; no non-controlling interest on the balance sheet.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF DCF (component route) + non-US/cyclical adaptations (owner-fcf-adaptations.md) -- operating company (global RV/campervan build-rent-sell + NZ tourism attractions), NZD reporter, NZX/ASX dual-listed, cyclical Sell segment. Fresh build (no prior THL.NZ DCF or Drivers file existed). FY0 = FY2026 CONTINUING OPERATIONS revenue (NZ$852.871m), not the NZ$885.261m total-group figure, because the UK & Ireland business was divested 31 Mar 2026 and is presented as discontinued -- carrying the discontinued revenue forward would project a business that no longer exists. KEY STRUCTURAL POINT: this business's fleet build/rent/sell cash cycle (gross fleet capex NZ$226.1m vs NBV of ex-fleet assets sold NZ$96.1m, net NZ$130.0m/yr) is classified under NZ IAS 7 as an OPERATING cash flow (netted inside 'receipts from customers' / 'purchase of rental assets'), not as investing capex against a matching D&A charge in the conventional SaaS/industrial sense. The reported 'CapEx' CSV line (NZ$13.0m) is NON-FLEET PP&E+intangibles only. The forward capex_pct_path therefore blends net fleet reinvestment (currently ~15% of revenue, moderating from the FY24-26 Australasian fleet regrowth peak toward a lower maintenance level as management has guided FY27 gross fleet capex 'broadly consistent' with FY26) with the small non-fleet capex line -- this is the single most important modelling choice for this ticker and is why owner-FCF margin ramps from ~2.7% (Y1) to ~8.5% (Y10) rather than starting near the historical actual. Historical growth CAGRs are NOT the primary anchor here: revenue CAGR is distorted by the FY2023 UK (Just Go/Bunk) acquisition roughly doubling group revenue then the FY2026 UK&I divestment reversing it; reported FCF was structurally NEGATIVE FY2022-FY2025 during the fleet regrowth/UK integration phase and only turned positive in FY2026 as fleet capex fell ($226m from $287m) -- neither series is a usable growth/margin anchor, so the forward build is anchored instead to FY2026 component actuals (underlying EBITDA margin 26.1% continuing, lease and D&A-ex-ROU ratios, net fleet capex ratio) and management's own stated targets (15% ROFE through-the-cycle vs 8.7% delivered FY2026; NZ$100m annualised NPAT Growth Roadmap goal, whose timing management has explicitly disclosed has been pushed out by Middle East conflict disruption to FY27 booking intake). Cash tax rate ramped from FY2026's distorted 35.2% effective rate (inflated by non-deductible takeover transaction costs and US/UK deferred-tax-asset derecognition) down to a blended-jurisdiction normalised ~28% (NZ statutory 28%, Australia 30%, US/Canada lower, weighted toward NZ/Australia post the UK exit). No interest-income stripping needed -- THL is a net-DEBT company (net debt NZ$434.9m ex-lease), not net-cash; the NZ$0.658m of interest received is immaterial and left in the flows. SBC is genuinely near-zero (0.16% of revenue) -- rows kept explicit per house rule; house and street bases are within rounding of each other given the tiny SBC base (band_position reported, not forced to null, since SBC is nonzero, just small). TAKEOVER CONTEXT (not substituted for intrinsic value): as of 2026-09-26 two non-binding, conditional indicative proposals remain live -- BGH Capital/Trouchet consortium at NZ$3.10/share and an Indie Campers-identified strategic bidder at NZ$3.30-3.40/share -- both in due diissance since mid-2026, no board recommendation or binding scheme as of this valuation date, and the Trouchet/BGH cooperation lock-up has been extended to 31 March 2027 (a signal the process may run long, not a deadline for due diligence itself). Per SKILL.md routing, a live corporate action normally breaks the three-scenario growth frame in favour of deal-completes-vs-deal-breaks weighting; here the instruction is to build the standalone intrinsic-value DCF as the primary artefact (the model below) and treat the indicative price range as context in the narrative/philosophy rather than as a valuation input -- the Board's own stated view of intrinsic value ('well north of $3.00 per share', Aug 2025) and the live bid range are reported as external reference points, not scenario drivers. If either proposal converts to a binding scheme this DCF should be revisited and a deal-probability overlay added.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: component build anchored to FY2026 actuals and management guidance, NOT a historical CAGR (see rationale)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs are not usable growth anchors for this ticker. Revenue 3yr/5yr CAGRs (10.1%/19.8%) are inflated by the FY2023 UK (Just Go/Bunk) acquisition, which roughly doubled group revenue overnight, and then partially reversed by the 31-Mar-2026 UK&I divestment -- neither end of either CAGR window describes the current, smaller, continuing-operations business. EPS and FCF CAGRs are not meaningful: EPS swung from -$9.20 (FY2021) to -$1.00 (FY2022) to +$26.40 (FY2023) to +$18.17 (FY2024) to -$11.72 (FY2025) to +$17.38 (FY2026), and owner FCF was negative every year FY2022-FY2025 (fleet regrowth + UK integration) before turning positive in FY2026 -- a CAGR through sign changes is undefined and reported as null rather than a misleading number. Equity 3yr CAGR (1.6%) is distorted by the FY2023 capital raise (shares 151.99m -> 189.01m to fund the UK acquisition) diluting per-share book value growth even as absolute equity grew; equity 5yr CAGR (15.4%) spans both the raise and the FY2025 loss. The selected_growth_rate of 6.0% is the base-case Year-1 revenue growth rate from the component build (anchored to FY2026 continuing-operations actuals, the Growth Roadmap's rental-led growth thesis, and management's guidance that RV sales are cyclically -- not structurally -- depressed), not a historical CAGR.

base.narrative: Base case: the Growth Roadmap continues to deliver but on the slower timeline management itself has now disclosed. Rentals -- the 'engine' of the business -- keep compounding at high-single/mid-single digits as Australasian and Canadian forward bookings recover from the March 2026 Middle East disruption and North America's 'one fleet' synergies mature past breakeven. The RV sales (Sell) segment is treated as cyclically, not structurally, depressed: volumes stabilise then recover gradually over 3-4 years as affordability pressure eases (consistent with management's and industry participants' own framing), pulling underlying EBITDA margin from FY2026's 26.1% (continuing) toward a mid-cycle 27.5%. Net fleet reinvestment -- currently the dominant cash cost at ~15% of revenue post the Australasian fleet-regrowth programme -- moderates toward an 11.5% steady-state maintenance level as management's guidance that FY27 gross fleet capex stays 'broadly consistent' with FY26 gives way to a genuine capex plateau once the fleet stops growing as fast as revenue. ROFE improves toward, but does not reach, the 15% through-the-cycle target within the 10-year window; the $100m annualised NPAT goal is achieved only toward the end of the horizon, later than management's original 3-4-year framing, consistent with their own disclosed timeline slippage.

bull.narrative: Bull case: the RV sales cycle turns faster than management expects -- THOR/Camping World-style industry conditions normalise within 12-18 months rather than staying depressed -- while rental growth stays strong across all four geographic segments as inbound tourism keeps recovering and the Middle East-related booking gap proves recoverable rather than permanent. North America's 'one fleet' synergies compound quickly past breakeven toward a normal-margin contribution, Action Manufacturing's consolidation delivers the full targeted Brisbane sublease saving plus further procurement gains, and underlying EBITDA margin expands to ~29.5% as fixed-cost leverage kicks in on a larger, better-utilised fleet. Fleet capex normalises faster (revenue growth outpaces fleet growth once the Australasian regrowth phase is fully behind the company), driving ROFE toward the 15% through-the-cycle target and the $100m annualised NPAT Growth Roadmap goal being achieved within or close to management's original 3-4-year window. A modestly lower WACC (8.5%) reflects the balance-sheet deleveraging this path implies.

bear.narrative: Bear case: the RV sales downturn proves partly structural rather than purely cyclical -- affordability pressure, EV/alternative-travel substitution and a permanently smaller pool of first-time RV buyers keep sale-of-goods revenue depressed for years, echoing the risk that industry participants (RVIA, THOR, Camping World) have cut 2026 forecasts repeatedly through the year rather than just once. Geopolitical shocks recur or the Middle East disruption's booking-intake gap proves genuinely unrecoverable as management itself has flagged, capping rental growth at low-single digits. North America stays stuck near breakeven (its FY2026 ROFE was only 0.5%) rather than compounding past it, Australia's improvement stalls, and margin stays pinned near 24% as fixed costs (leases, depreciation on an ageing, slower-growing fleet) do not get the operating leverage the base case assumes. Fleet capex stays structurally elevated for longer because management is forced to keep replacing an ageing fleet even as unit economics disappoint, keeping leverage near or above the current 2.3x and the 15% ROFE target and $100m NPAT goal permanently out of reach within the horizon. A higher WACC (9.5%) reflects sustained leverage and earnings unpredictability (as evidenced by the FY2026 guidance round-trips).

scenario_narratives.base: Rental-led recovery on the slower timeline management itself has now disclosed; RV sales treated as cyclical, gradually normalising; fleet capex moderates toward a maintenance level as the Australasian regrowth programme completes.
scenario_narratives.bull: RV sales cycle turns faster than expected, rental growth stays strong across all segments, North America and manufacturing synergies compound quickly, and the $100m NPAT Growth Roadmap goal is achieved close to its original 3-4-year timeline.
scenario_narratives.bear: RV sales downturn proves partly structural, geopolitical disruption to bookings recurs or the March-2026 gap proves permanently unrecoverable, North America stays near breakeven, and fleet capex stays structurally elevated -- the 15% ROFE target and $100m NPAT goal stay out of reach within the horizon.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight lifted from the house default 15% to 25% because: (1) the RV sales (Sell) segment has now missed industry expectations repeatedly through calendar 2026 (RVIA cutting its wholesale shipment forecast 11% mid-year, THOR and Camping World both cutting guidance further), which is exactly the pattern that precedes a downturn proving partly structural rather than purely cyclical; (2) management's own FY2026 guidance round-tripped twice in one year (underlying NPAT $43-47m -> $40-43m -> ~$46m; net debt <$400m -> $460-470m -> $435.5m), evidencing real forecasting difficulty; (3) North America ROFE remains near breakeven (0.5%) after several years of stated turnaround effort. Bull weight trimmed to 25% (from the 35% default) because it requires several largely independent things to go right at once -- a faster-than-guided RV sales recovery, North America clearing breakeven convincingly, and the Middle East booking gap proving fully recoverable rather than partially permanent as management has already flagged. Base holds the house default 50%. This weighting is independent of, and does not incorporate, the live non-binding takeover approaches (NZ$3.10-3.40/share) -- those are reported as external context in valuation_philosophy, not folded into the probability-weighted standalone intrinsic value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: This is a standalone, intrinsic-value owner-FCF DCF for a cyclical, capital-intensive, vertically-integrated (build/rent/sell) global RV rental and NZ tourism-attraction operator, built on FY2026 continuing-operations actuals following the 31-March-2026 divestment of the UK & Ireland business. The single most important modelling judgment is that this business's dominant cash flow item -- the fleet build/rent/sell cycle (gross fleet capex NZ$226m vs NZ$96m NBV of ex-fleet assets sold, net ~NZ$130m/yr, currently ~15% of revenue) -- sits inside operating cash flow under NZ IAS 7 rather than as conventional capex against a matching D&A line, and is modelled as an explicit, moderating capex_pct path rather than assumed away or conflated with accounting D&A. Historical revenue/EPS/FCF CAGRs are not usable anchors here (the FY2023 UK acquisition roughly doubled revenue, the FY2026 UK&I divestment partially reversed it, and owner FCF was structurally negative FY2022-FY2025 during the fleet regrowth phase) -- the forward build is instead anchored to FY2026 component actuals and management's own stated targets (15% through-the-cycle ROFE vs 8.7% delivered; the NZ$100m annualised NPAT Growth Roadmap goal, whose timing management has explicitly disclosed has slipped). IMPORTANT CONTEXT NOT USED AS A VALUATION INPUT: as of this valuation date (26 September 2026), thl is the subject of two live, non-binding, conditional indicative takeover proposals -- NZ$3.10/share from a BGH Capital/Trouchet family consortium and NZ$3.30-3.40/share from a strategic bidder industry sources identify as Indie Campers -- both in due diligence, with no board recommendation or binding scheme as of this date, and a Trouchet/BGH cooperation lock-up now extended to 31 March 2027 (a sign the process could run well into next year rather than resolve imminently). The Board's own August 2025 stated view that fair value is 'well north of $3.00 per share' and the live bid range are genuine, market-tested reference points and are reported here for context, but per house methodology a live corporate action normally calls for a deal-completes-vs-deal-breaks weighting rather than a standard three-scenario growth DCF; this build deliberately keeps the two separate -- the probability-weighted intrinsic value below is the standalone fundamental case, not a blend with the takeover price. A reader should treat the gap between the two (if the intrinsic value comes in below the indicative bid range, which is expected given the bids sit above the Board's own pre-takeover valuation view) as the price of the takeover-completion optionality, not as a model error.
key_risks_to_valuation: Takeover process resolution risk: if both non-binding proposals lapse (as the original NZ$2.30/share BGH approach did in 2025), the stock could de-rate from the current price (see current_price/price_as_of) toward the standalone intrinsic value computed here, which this model expects to sit below the current price given the bid-range overhang -- verify current takeover status via NZX/ASX announcements before acting on this valuation

RV sales (Sell) segment cyclicality proving structural rather than cyclical -- affordability pressure, EV/alternative-travel substitution, and a smaller pool of first-time RV buyers could permanently impair the Sell segment's contribution and the vertically-integrated build/rent/sell economics that depend on efficient fleet churn

Fleet capex does not moderate as guided -- if gross fleet capex fails to fall toward a genuine maintenance level as the Australasian regrowth programme completes, owner FCF margin stays permanently depressed versus the base case's ramp to ~8.5%
North America fails to clear breakeven (FY2026 ROFE only 0.5%) -- a persistent drag that could keep group ROFE below the 15% target and the $100m NPAT goal out of reach indefinitely

Recurring geopolitical/macro shocks to international travel demand (the March 2026 Middle East conflict is the most recent example) directly disrupt booking intake and RV sales in a way management itself says may not be 'fully recoverable'
FX translation risk across NZD/AUD/USD/CAD and interest-rate sensitivity on a moderately leveraged (2.32x underlying EBITDA ex-lease) balance sheet
